name: manual_8df4d1
claim: On macOS/BSD, singleton daemon-start locks in shell scripts must use mkdir-is-atomic + rm -rf for teardown, never flock(1) or rmdir.

decisions.notes: flock(1) is util-linux-only and absent on macOS by default — a flock-based fix silently fails on the exact platform being debugged. Separately, rmdir silently no-ops on a non-empty lock directory; if the lock dir ever contains a pid marker file (the normal case), every successful run leaves the lock behind and the next daemon restart spins forever in the reclaim loop. Found while fixing orama-system exa-mcp-wrapper.sh: reproduced both the daemon-start race (5 concurrent launches -> 2 competing daemons, 0/5 responses) and the rmdir infinite-loop regression (clean run then forced restart hung indefinitely, exit 124) with concrete tests before and after each fix. A second independent reviewer (parallel Sonnet 5 + GLM-5.2 review) caught the rmdir bug that the first fix pass missed.
